 WebMCP DevTools 

 Why your use case is a strong fit for WebMCP 

 Browser agents need safe, specific context—not brittle screen-scraping guesses. WebMCP lets a page expose exactly the developer tools an agent needs. 

 How it creates a better user experience 

 Developers stay in their normal browser workflow while agents inspect, diagnose, and verify work through clear, bounded tools with useful evidence. 

 Describe what people and agents can do together that was difficult or impossible before 

 People set intent and approve changes. Agents can find an element, read safe page state, surface errors, interact with allowed controls, and run a same-page test—without DevTools handoffs. 

 Briefly explain how you implemented WebMCP 

 We define Zod contracts first, register tools through document.modelContext , and keep DOM access behind adapters. Inputs are validated, outputs are bounded, and mutations require explicit permission.
